doc.title: Frank Alkyer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Orleans, Louisiana, January 10, 2020

chapter: Remembering writers and stories behind the magazine
title: Biggest disasters and missed opportunities: Tito Puente, B.B. King and Les Paul
summary: Alkyer cites missed chances: no Tito Puente cover after his death, and a B.B. King and Les Paul conversation that fell through. He recalls no real disasters.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I don’t know if you’d share this with me but what’s the biggest, most significant disaster you’ve had in your tenure at DownBeat, with some kind of article or a mistake.
Wow. There have been a few. The biggest disaster.

You know this is interesting, I rarely ask this question with musicians and I tried it a bunch of times, and the question was, “What’s the worst gig you ever played.” And I don’t know if anybody’s ever actually answered it. And if at all it usually isn’t something about the music, it’s more like the bus broke down — it’s a non-musical thing. © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

Right, right, right. Well for me there are things that didn’t happen. Things that we tried to do, all right — this is just, to this day, oh, things that didn’t happen. I loved Tito Puente. I got to spend time with him, got to know him, I loved his music before that, I loved it after that, I loved Tito Puente. And the timing of his death was such that it would have been great stress on the staff to put him on the cover, and putting him on the next cover would have been too far away. So it was just — and I wish we’d have ripped up the issue and done it. We should have put Tito on the cover of the magazine when he passed away. A missed opportunity. There was another one where B.B. King and Les Paul are in New York City. B.B. is going to play a gig in New York City, Les is in New York City. We wanted to get B.B. King and Les Paul together to do a conversation because they both had great respect for each other. I thought this was a brilliant idea. B.B. wanted Les to go five blocks south to his hotel to do the interview. Les wanted B.B. to go five blocks north to Iridium to do the interview. We offered a limo either way, it didn’t matter, either way we were willing to do it. The negotiations lasted about two weeks. We could not get either one of them to budge from their position and had to abandon this article, and it’s just like ahhh. I would have loved to have that. These two giants of their respective genres of the art form together to talk about it. So that is a missed opportunity. I don’t think, the disasters are like not really disasters, just people not doing their job so we’ve got to be there until two o’clock in the morning or things like that. You know, it’s the stuff that goes on behind the curtain that we don’t want you to see. I can’t remember like doing something, we’ve made mistakes, we’ve had to correct things in the magazine, but I can’t remember something that I’d go yeah we really screwed things up there. Most of it was just something happened on the back end and we had to scramble or just work inordinate hours to get the product out and make sure it was still good.
